note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management following recent PSA elevation and prior biopsy diagnosis.

The patient is a 64-year-old widowed small business owner (cafe) living independently in a retirement community. He has a medical history of hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, COPD, and osteoarthritis, managed with amlodipine, metoprolol, atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, tiotropium, and salbutamol PRN. He is a current smoker with a 21 pack-year history and consumes approximately 5 units of alcohol weekly. He engages in gardening but does not perform structured exercise. His IPSS score is 1/35, indicating mild lower urinary tract symptoms. He reports no recent bone pain, haematuria, or unexplained weight loss. His adult daughter serves as his primary next-of-kin contact.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals stable vital signs with a blood pressure of 121/85 mmHg and heart rate of 72 bpm. The patient's BMI is 28.7 kg/m2.
